$comment: LW-WATCHTOWER module switchboard, and THE SHIPPED DEFAULTS - do not edit this file to configure the plugin. Claude Code has no per-hook disable - disableAllHooks is all-or-nothing and would also kill the status line - so every module gates itself on the flags below. Since 3 September 2026 (#11) an operator setting goes to config.override.json under the state directory ($CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA, or ~/.claude/plugins/data/lw-watchtower*/), which Get-LwgConfig merges over these defaults, and /lw-watchtower:config and /lw-watchtower:delegate write that file for you. THIS file is tracked and lives inside the plugin's own git working tree, so editing it dirties the checkout and makes /lw-watchtower:update refuse to pull - which is the defect the override exists to fix. An edit here still takes effect where no override overrides it, and no reinstall is needed either way, because the plugin is loaded through a directory junction.

$status.$comment: READ THIS BEFORE THE FLAGS BELOW. A flag set to true is a forward-declaration of intent, NOT evidence that any code exists. Anything listed under "planned" would be a name with no behaviour behind it, and switching such a name on or off changes nothing. "planned" is EMPTY as of 30 July 2026 - every flag in the `modules` block is backed by code and enabled, and the gates are backed by code and switched OFF - and the rule stands anyway, because it is the rule that keeps the count honest the next time a name is added ahead of its code. THERE IS ONE AUTHORITATIVE LIST AND IT IS NOT IN THIS FILE: $LwgModuleRegistry in lib/common.ps1. The SessionStart banner reads it, bin/lwg-doctor.ps1's config-registry check holds the `modules` block below to it, and Get-LwgImplementedModules answers 'which modules are built' from it for anything that asks. HOW MANY THERE ARE OF ANYTHING IS DELIBERATELY NOT STATED HERE (#195): a count written in this file is a copy that nothing derives and nothing checks, and it goes stale the next time a module is added. docs/modules.md renders the registry and tests/doc_claims.ps1 holds that page to it.
$status.$removed_implemented_comment: AN "implemented" ARRAY USED TO SIT ON THIS LINE, naming every module in the registry a second time, and it was DELETED ON 3 SEPTEMBER 2026 (#75) rather than wired to a check. The removal is recorded here rather than left to be inferred from an absence. NOTHING IN THE TREE EVER READ IT - not bin/lwg-doctor.ps1's config-registry check, which compares the `modules` keys against $LwgModuleRegistry and the declared switch keys and never looked at this array; not any rule in tests/doc_claims.ps1; not any hook - while the comment beside it told the next reader that the array and the `modules` block were kept in step for them. A hand-maintained copy of the registry, believed because a comment named a check that does not exist, is a stale list wearing the authority of a checked one: add a module, forget this array, and CI stays green while the file quietly reports the wrong number. That is the shape this plugin exists to catch - a switch wired to nothing - so the copy went instead of gaining a check nobody asked for. What the array's own comment was RIGHT about is kept, because it is a real property of the `modules` block and not a count: the gate and supervision modules are deliberately ABSENT from it, because each declares its own switch (interaction.delegate for delegate_gate; the `supervision` block further down for the rest) on its registry entry via the `switch` field. A second flag over the same module would let an operator turn it on with a command and have it silently do nothing, and Get-LwgConfig fails OPEN - a corrupt config must never arm a blocking gate. Which modules those are is in $LwgModuleRegistry and rendered in docs/modules.md; it is not restated here (#195).
$status.$planned_comment: EMPTY, and that is now the honest answer: every name in the `modules` block below is backed by code. It used to hold ratelimit_escalation and cost_tracking; both were removed on 30 July 2026 at the owner's instruction - see $removed_blocked_comment. The key is kept rather than deleted so that a future unbuilt module has somewhere to be declared without inventing the convention again.
$status.$default_off_comment: EMPTY, and it stays empty because this key only ever described the `modules` block below - every flag in that block is built and enabled. context_pressure was deleted on 6 September 2026 with #168 and the transition ladder replaced it as a layer of effort_ledger rather than as a module of its own. THE REGISTRY IS NO LONGER ALL-ENABLED, and that is not a contradiction: delegate_gate (flag interaction.delegate) and the supervision gates send_liveness_gate and completion_audit (flags in the `supervision` block) ship built and switched OFF, and none of their flags is a `modules` key, so none is a member of the list this one is about. They are named here anyway, because 'default_off is empty' would otherwise read as 'nothing ships off', which is not true. How many ship enabled and how many ship off is derived from the `modules` block below and from $LwgModuleRegistry, rendered in docs/modules.md, and asserted by tests/doc_claims.ps1 - it is not written out here (#195).
$status.$self_health_comment: self_health honours its flag. Set it to false and the SessionStart self-check does not run at all - no probe, no config-parsed assertion, no state-dir write test. The banner and the model-visible context then report mode 'unverified' and say in words that nothing was checked. They deliberately do NOT say 'enforcing', 'partial' or 'observe-only': those three all assert that the self-check passed, and asserting that on the strength of a check that never ran is the same lie as counting an unbuilt module as coverage. 'degraded' would be the opposite lie - it claims a probe failed, and none did.
$status.$context_injection_comment: context_injection is the SubagentStart hook (lib/subagent_start.ps1). Claude Code snapshots CLAUDE.md into a subagent's context at PARENT-SESSION start, so an instruction added mid-session never reaches a worker dispatched later - a security classifier here once refused a legitimate edit because its snapshot predated the instruction authorising it. SubagentStart fires per dispatch, so what it emits is always current. It injects context/worker_facts.md as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext, reading that file live every time; edit the file and the next dispatch picks it up with no code change. Facts only, and short - every dispatch pays for the text. Set this to false and the hook emits nothing and exits 0. ONE PROCESS SERVES THIS MODULE AND effort_ledger, AND THIS FLAG DOES NOT SWITCH THE OTHER: since 6 September 2026 lib/subagent_start.ps1 also appends the START half of the dispatch record to health.jsonl, and that write is gated on effort_ledger, not on this key. context_injection false still writes the row; effort_ledger false stops the row and still injects. The row's measured cost was ACCEPTED rather than absorbed - most of it is Windows PowerShell 5.1 compiling a longer file, so it is charged even with effort_ledger off. The word ceiling, the measured cost and the module counts all live where they are derived: docs/modules.md under effort_ledger, and docs/limitations.md (#195).
$status.$removed_blocked_comment: ratelimit_escalation and cost_tracking WERE declared here as 'planned'. Both were REMOVED ON 30 JULY 2026 by an explicit owner decision, and the removal is recorded here rather than left to be inferred from an absence: a name that can never be built is not a plan, and carrying it in a switchboard invites someone to switch it on. THE REASON THEY CANNOT BE BUILT IS NOT DELETED WITH THEM - it lives in docs/modules.md under 'Attempted and blocked: ratelimit_escalation and cost_tracking', in full, with the field-by-field evidence, so that nobody re-attempts them. In one line: verified against the claude-code 2.1.220 binary, rate_limits / cost / context_window / workspace are assembled in exactly ONE place, the status-line input builder, and no hook event carries any of them. DO NOT ADD EITHER NAME BACK to the modules block below without first reading that section; a flag with no reachable data behind it is the precise defect this plugin exists to catch. The status line already colours rate-limit usage and prints its 'land all work' advisory, because that is the one process that receives the data - see thresholds.ratelimit below.
$status.$gates_comment: EVERY GATE THIS PLUGIN SHIPS IS SWITCHED OFF. A `gates_live` integer used to sit above this line asserting how many were live; it was DELETED because nothing computed it, nothing validated it and nothing updated it - it went false inside this very file the moment an operator set interaction.delegate to true, which is the one supported way to arm a gate. Get-LwgActiveGates answers the live count from the registry and the switches, correctly, for anything that asks. The LIVE / SHIPPED distinction the number tried to carry is still the whole point: delegate_gate (PreToolUse on Edit|Write|NotebookEdit|Bash, switch interaction.delegate), send_liveness_gate (PreToolUse on SendMessage, switch supervision.send_liveness) and completion_audit (a Stop entry with no asyncRewake, switch supervision.completion_audit) are each declared in $LwgModuleRegistry with kind 'gate', each registered in hooks/hooks.json, and each blocks nothing at all until its own switch is set to true. Turn one on and the count rises, Get-LwgActiveGates returns it, and the session mode leaves 'observe-only' - all of that follows from the registry fields with no other edit. Every OTHER module is kind 'observe': it reports, logs or advises, and the action happens regardless. HISTORY: destructive_gate and then secret_scan were removed on 30 July 2026 at the owner's instruction, leaving no gate of any kind; delegate_gate was built later the same day as the only gate then fully buildable, and send_liveness_gate and completion_audit were built 1 August 2026 from the measured queued-message-reported-as-done failure recorded in the `supervision` block's $comment. THE TRIP LEDGER DID NOT COME BACK WITH ANY OF THEM - a denial is recorded in lw-watchtower.jsonl as a GateDeny event and nothing tracks it as an open item. Read docs/gates-removed.md before adding another gate - it records why the first two went, what the failed fix attempts taught, and the rules a new gate has to follow; the newer gates, like delegate_gate, parse no shell and decide nothing about whether content is safe. How many gates there are is derived from $LwgModuleRegistry and rendered in docs/modules.md (#195).
$status.$removed_comment: destructive_gate WAS the second live gate - a PreToolUse hook on Bash|PowerShell (lib/gate_bash.ps1) refusing force pushes, hard resets, history rewrites, recursive deletes and GitHub repo destruction, plus a path half in the since-deleted lib/gate_write.ps1 refusing writes inside a .git directory. It was REMOVED ON 30 JULY 2026 by an explicit owner decision, and the removal is recorded here rather than left to be inferred from an absence. NOTHING in this plugin inspects a shell command any more, and no write to .git internals is refused by any hook. The permissions.deny mirror went in the same change: bin/lwg-setup.ps1 dropped the git-destructive, filesystem-destructive, github-destructive and git-internals groups (133 of 181 rules), so a fresh install has neither a hook layer nor a config layer for destructive commands. A machine set up before that date still carries the old rules in its own settings.json and the CLI still evaluates them; nothing here renews them. The code is recoverable from git history; see CHANGELOG.md for the commits. <!-- doc-claims:ignore -->
$status.$removed_secret_comment: secret_scan WAS the last gate, and it was REMOVED ON 30 JULY 2026 by an explicit owner decision, in the same spirit as the destructive gate above and recorded here rather than left to be inferred. It was a PreToolUse hook on Write|Edit|NotebookEdit (lib/gate_write.ps1, now DELETED) that refused writes to credential paths - *.pem, *.key, id_rsa*, .env and friends - and writes whose CONTENT carried a live GitHub, AWS or Slack token. Both halves are gone: no hook inspects the path being written and no hook inspects the bytes being written. Its permissions.deny mirror went in the same change - bin/lwg-setup.ps1 dropped the secret-paths and secret-reads groups, the last 48 of the original 181 rules - so the deny table the installer writes is now EMPTY and a fresh install has neither a hook layer nor a config layer for credentials. Nothing this plugin ships can stop a secret reaching disk. A machine set up before that date still carries the 48 rules in its own settings.json unless they were removed by hand; nothing here renews them. THE TRIP LEDGER WENT THE SAME DAY, AFTER THE GATES: lib/trips.ps1, lib/ack_trip.ps1, bin/lwg-tripped.ps1 and commands/tripped.md were kept for a few hours as readers for the per-session ledgers already on disk, and were then removed with those ledgers by a further explicit owner decision. The ledger files were backed up before deletion, not destroyed. Nothing now records, reads, closes or acknowledges a trip, and a future gate has to rebuild the whole format - see docs/gates-removed.md. The code is recoverable from git history; see CHANGELOG.md for the commits. <!-- doc-claims:ignore -->

interaction.$comment: INTERACTION PREFERENCES. The key here is `delegate`. It is absent from the `modules` block above for the same reason `output_style` is - a corrupt config must not be able to flip it, because Get-LwgConfig fails OPEN and would switch on a blocking gate nobody asked for - but it is NOT merely a preference any more. Since 30 July 2026 it is the switch on delegate_gate, a real PreToolUse gate, and $LwgModuleRegistry in lib/common.ps1 carries a `delegate_gate` entry whose `switch` field names this exact key. That is why there is no second flag for it in `modules`: a second switch over the same gate lets an operator turn it on with the command and have it silently do nothing, which is the founding defect this plugin exists to catch. bin/lwg-doctor.ps1's config-registry check asserts that this key is present here and that the registry entry points at it.
interaction.$removed_keys_comment: `ask` and `ask_inline` WERE HERE, defaulting to true, and both were REMOVED ON 30 JULY 2026 by an explicit owner decision. The removal is recorded here rather than left to be inferred from an absence, because both had been ON by default since they shipped while enforcing nothing at all. Neither can be built as specified: `ask` would need a Stop hook refusing to end a turn while an unanswered decision is outstanding, and a Stop hook can block turn-end but cannot stop prose from having already appeared and cannot detect a question that should have been asked and was not - so the half that matters is unreachable. `ask_inline` would need something that counts and merges the questions asked in a turn, and nothing can merge them after the fact; the 4-questions / 2-4-options shape was always a platform limit on the question tool rather than a rule this plugin applied. commands/ask.md and commands/ask-inline.md are deleted, bin/lwg-toggle.ps1 no longer accepts either name, and a flag left here would be a setting nothing reads. DO NOT ADD EITHER KEY BACK without a mechanism, not a hook name.
interaction.$delegate_comment: DEFAULT FALSE, AND IT SHIPS FALSE ON PURPOSE. Its on state changes how work is done without being asked, and shipping a blocking gate switched on by default is the opposite of what this plugin argues for everywhere else. Set it true - /lw-watchtower:delegate on - and lib/gate_delegate.ps1 refuses Edit, Write, NotebookEdit, Bash and PowerShell for any call that did not come from a subagent. PowerShell joined that list on 1 August 2026: this is a Windows-only plugin, the CLI offers both shell tools there, and the matcher named only one of them - so an armed gate could be walked round by asking for the other shell while /lw-watchtower:doctor reported it live. WHAT THAT COSTS, stated here rather than discovered: /lw-watchtower:delegate off will not work from the main thread afterwards, because that command runs its script through Bash and Bash is one of the five. There is deliberately no exemption for it. The two ways back are to have a subagent run the command, or to set this key to false by hand. An unreadable config leaves the gate OFF rather than on, which is the polarity that keeps a bad config a nuisance instead of a lockout.
interaction.$repo_override_comment: Per-repo overrides take the shape "repos": { "LEAPWare-Software/example-repo": { "interaction": { "delegate": true } } }, in a block alongside `modules`. Only the keys listed under a repo are overridden; everything else falls through to the default here. /lw-watchtower:delegate on repo writes that entry - into config.override.json under the state directory, NOT into this file (#11) - and creates the repo object if it is absent. A `repos` block written here by hand is still read: Get-LwgConfig merges the override over these defaults and lib/gate_delegate.ps1 honours the result, because the gate resolves its switch through the same Test-LwgModule the banner uses. So a per-repo override applies to a gate exactly as it applies to a module, from whichever file carries it.

supervision.$comment: COMPLETION-INTEGRITY GATES, BOTH OFF BY DEFAULT - and this block holds ONLY GATES since 8 September 2026 (#166) took orphan_watch out of it; see $removed_orphan_watch_comment below. Built 1 August 2026 from a measured failure: an orchestrator issued SendMessage to a subagent that had been DEAD FOR 28 MINUTES 45 SECONDS, read the 'Message queued for delivery' acknowledgement as done, and told the user 3.46 seconds later that a file had been updated which was never touched - while the health log read green, because Get-FailedTasks counts only failed/killed BACKGROUND TASKS and a subagent killed mid-flight produces no record anywhere (a cross-check found FOUR such orphans, against a log with zero PostToolUseFailure records in 1,175 entries). The keys live HERE and not in the `modules` block for the same reason interaction.delegate does: Get-LwgConfig fails OPEN, and a corrupt config must never arm a blocking gate nobody asked for. Each key is declared on its own registry entry in lib/common.ps1 via the `switch` field, bin/lwg-doctor.ps1 asserts the declared keys exist, and per-repo overrides go under `repos` exactly as for delegate: "repos": { "Owner/Name": { "supervision": { "send_liveness": true } } }.
supervision.$send_liveness_comment: send_liveness_gate (lib/gate_send.ps1), PreToolUse on SendMessage. ON: refuses a send whose recipient it can prove is dead mid-flight - transcript exists for this session, no SubagentStop record, transcript silent past module_config.send_liveness_gate.stale_minutes - and refuses a recipient that resolves to nothing at all. Abstains (allows, logged) on `name@team` addresses and on sessions health.jsonl never recorded. DO NOT ARM THIS in an agent-team workflow; it does not understand team layouts and will refuse bare teammate names it cannot resolve.
supervision.$completion_audit_comment: completion_audit (lib/gate_stop.ps1), a Stop entry registered WITHOUT asyncRewake, so its exit 2 BLOCKS the turn end. ON: refuses to end a turn whose final assistant text asserts completed work while the turn's last tool action was SendMessage - queued is not delivered, delivered is not done. Fires at most once per turn end (stop_hook_active stands it down on the continuation), so it forces one round of verification and cannot force honesty. Its claim detection is a stated regex over prose; read the false-positive/negative enumeration in lib/gate_stop.ps1 before arming it.
supervision.$removed_orphan_watch_comment: orphan_watch WAS THE THIRD KEY IN THIS BLOCK and it was REMOVED ON 8 SEPTEMBER 2026 (#166) - MERGED, not deleted. Every behaviour it named still runs, from the same lines of lib/supervisor.ps1, under modules.effort_ledger; its threshold moved to module_config.effort_ledger.stale_minutes. The removal is recorded here rather than left to be inferred from an absence, because this is a BREAKING config change and an operator arriving with supervision.orphan_watch in their config.override.json needs to find out from somewhere. WHAT THAT KEY NOW DOES: nothing. It is merged into the effective config, no registry entry declares it, so no code reads it - and unlike a stale key in the `modules` block, /lw-watchtower:doctor's config-registry row does NOT report it either, because that row enumerates the `modules` block for strays and has never enumerated this one. It is the silent half of the rename, which is exactly why it is written down here. WHY IT MERGED: it declared its own switch and sat BELOW the ledger's flag gate, so an operator could set it true and have it do nothing at all because the ledger was off - two switches over one data source, which is the switch-wired-to-nothing defect this plugin exists to catch. THE COST, STATED: the reconciliation now ships ON, where this key shipped OFF. See the CHANGELOG's 0.5.0 upgrade note.

repos.$comment: Per-repo overrides keyed by the 'owner/name' slug of the ORIGIN REMOTE. The slug is resolved from the hook payload's cwd - walk up for .git, read the origin url out of its config - because payload.workspace does NOT exist in any hook event; it is built only for the status line. Until this was fixed every hook resolved the repo to null and nothing in this block applied to anything. Keys are matched case-insensitively. Only the modules listed under a repo are overridden; everything else falls through to the global defaults above. Example: "LEAPWare-Software/example-repo": { "modules": { "docs_coupling": false } }

thresholds.$ratelimit_comment: Read by ~/.claude/statusline.ps1, which is the only process that receives rate_limits at all. There is no ratelimit_escalation module and there cannot be - it was removed on 30 July 2026 because no hook is given the data; see $status.$removed_blocked_comment and docs/modules.md. WHAT THESE TWO NUMBERS ACTUALLY DRIVE, corrected on 3 August 2026: the SECOND ROW only - whether the 'approaching limit' / 'land all work' advisory appears, which of the two texts it takes and which colour it is printed in. They do NOT colour the percentage on row 1. That colour comes from Heat(), which holds three fixed band edges at 50/75/90 and reads no configuration at all, so on the shipped defaults a rate limit turns red at 90 while the advisory still says 'approaching' until 92. The sentence here used to say these numbers drove 'the status line's colouring', and an operator who lowered them and watched the figure's colour saw nothing change.
thresholds.$context_comment: The same distinction as $ratelimit_comment, for the ctx segment: these two decide the advisory on row 2 and not the colour of the figure on row 1. A configured 0 is honoured and means 'always' - it used to be discarded as falsy - and a value that is not a number is named on the advisory row and the built-in below is used instead of it, rather than being swapped in silently. /lw-watchtower:doctor validates nothing under thresholds.
thresholds.$ladder_comment: THE TRANSITION LADDER (#168), read by lib/supervisor.ps1's Stop branch through Get-LwgLadderTier in lib/common.ps1. These are TUNING, not a switch: the ladder has no flag of its own and rides effort_ledger's, which is stated in that module's registry entry. It reads signals/ratelimit.json - written by the STATUS LINE on every render, because no hook is handed rate_limits or context_window - and takes the WORST of five_hour, seven_day and context_window.used_percentage. At amber the model is told to start nothing new; at red it is told to land the work and run /lw-watchtower:lw-handoff. THESE NUMBERS ARE DELIBERATELY EARLIER THAN thresholds.ratelimit AND thresholds.context ABOVE, and the two sets are NOT the same knob: writing and auditing a handoff costs tokens and has to finish before the wall, so the ladder warns at 70/85 while the status line's own row-2 advisory still uses 88/92 and 75/90. Moving one does not move the other, and this issue deliberately did not move the status line's - that would change what the operator SEES on a path no case in this repository measures. There is no black tier yet; see the ladder block in lib/supervisor.ps1 for why. max_age_minutes is the STALENESS BUDGET: a signals/ratelimit.json older than this reports UNAVAILABLE and the previous turn's tier is never reused, because a monitor that fails silent turns 'I do not know' into 'I am fine'. A turn whose last tool call ran longer than this budget ends with a file the ladder calls stale, and that is the intended answer rather than a bug - raise the number if this operator's turns routinely run longer. /lw-watchtower:doctor validates nothing under thresholds.

module_config.$comment: Per-module tuning, read through Get-LwgModuleOption. Separate from `thresholds`, which is only the two numeric pressure groups. Every key here is optional: the code carries the same defaults, so deleting this block changes nothing.

git_hygiene.$comment: The ONLY module allowed to spawn a subprocess, and it does so on Stop only - never per render and never on PreToolUse, so it cannot delay or hang a tool call. Outside a git repo it spawns nothing at all. The common case is one `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch`, which answers dirty / detached / ahead / behind together; it also carries the unmerged (`u`) lines, which is where an unresolved conflict is now read from at no extra cost. A half-finished rebase, merge, cherry-pick or bisect and a forgotten stash are read with Test-Path against the git directory and spawn NOTHING, so they are still reported on a machine where git is missing or hanging - measured at about 1.2 percent of one git spawn on a dev box and 5.7 percent on a hosted runner, which is a reading of the machine as much as of the code - so case B37 of tests/stop_behaviour.ps1 now holds them to a budget counted in file checks rather than in spawns (#337). There is no flag for that half: it costs nothing to leave on and switching it off would only make the module quieter about the states it is least able to see any other way. a second `git rev-list` runs only on a branch with no upstream. A git command that times out, is missing or exits nonzero is reported as UNKNOWN - never as a clean tree. timeout_ms bounds each git call, gh_timeout_ms the one optional network call. use_gh false disables the open-PR check entirely; when true it still only runs where it can matter (unpushed work on a non-default branch) and is asked at most once per branch head per session. default_branches is the fallback used when refs/remotes/origin/HEAD is absent, which is normal in a repo that was created rather than cloned.

stack_mode.$comment: THE MODULE SHIPS SWITCHED OFF - see the `modules` block above, where its flag is false, and turn it on with /lw-watchtower:config once you have set the roots below. It is off for the reason this tree switches every new module off: it has never run in a live session, so nothing here has observed the CLI merging what it injects. Two further reasons are specific to it and are stated rather than left to be found - with both root lists empty it would resolve to the default and inject a PROTO pointer nobody asked for, which is cost with no function; and it is a SECOND PowerShell process on SubagentStart beside lib/subagent_start.ps1, so a dispatch pays a whole interpreter start again. docs/limitations.md carries that number. Which working discipline a session gets, and where. `ship_roots` and `proto_roots` are lists of path prefixes matched against the session's working directory on WHOLE PATH SEGMENTS, so a root does not capture a sibling directory that merely shares its opening characters; `default` is what a directory under neither list gets. Both lists ship EMPTY and the default ships proto, so nothing here changes anything until an operator says where their release trees are. THE ORDER THESE ARE CONSULTED IN IS NOT WRITTEN HERE and is not a matter of taste: the CLAUDE_STACK_MODE environment variable outranks a .stackmode marker in the working directory, which outranks these lists, which outrank `default`. That ladder is in $LwgModuleRegistry in lib/common.ps1 and in docs/modules.md, which is where a reader can also find why SHIP wins where the two lists overlap and what a root written relative, or through a junction, will and will not match. Setting `default` to off, or CLAUDE_STACK_MODE to off, injects nothing while leaving the module switched on.

send_liveness_gate.$comment: stale_minutes divides 'presumed running' from 'dead mid-flight' for a recipient with no SubagentStop record. Default 15, floor 1, and the default sits ABOVE the 10-minute Bash tool ceiling on purpose: an agent inside one long tool call writes nothing to its transcript for the length of the call, and a threshold under that ceiling would refuse sends to agents that are merely busy. The measured dead recipient had been silent 28m45s.

effort_ledger.$comment: Same number, same reasoning, applied to the transcript reconciliation instead of the send path. The two are separate knobs deliberately: an operator can make the alert patient while keeping the gate strict, or the reverse. THIS IS THE ONLY THRESHOLD, and a death the HARNESS has named does not serve it at all - see $removed_error_stale_comment. THIS BLOCK WAS KEYED orphan_watch UNTIL 8 SEPTEMBER 2026 (#166); the module merged into effort_ledger and its threshold came with it under the new name, so a config.override.json still spelling module_config.orphan_watch.stale_minutes sets nothing and the reconciliation runs on the 15 below.
effort_ledger.$removed_error_stale_comment: error_stale_minutes WAS a second, five-minute threshold for a transcript whose last record was an isApiErrorMessage, on the reasoning that a stated cause need not wait out inferred silence, with rate_limit and 529 excluded as back-pressure. IT WAS REMOVED ON 10 AUGUST 2026 BECAUSE IT WAS MEASURED REPORTING A LIVE AGENT DEAD, and the removal is recorded here rather than left to be inferred from an absence. Re-derived over 1,050 transcripts, all four mid-file API errors RECOVERED, with gaps 25.4s, 93.8s, 3,824.0s and 4,011.2s. The 4,011.2s one is error 'server_error' with NO apiErrorStatus and no '529' or 'Overloaded' anywhere in its text, so it fell through the class exclusion onto the five-minute path and would have been alerted as DIED while it went on working for another 62 minutes - one false positive in four. The threshold cannot be raised to fix it either: the longest live recovery is 66.85 MINUTES, longer than the 15-minute silence rule it existed to beat, so it bought nothing. What replaces it is better on both axes - the harness's own <status>failed</status> task-notification in the parent transcript, which is terminal by construction because a recovering agent is never given one, and which is believed with NO threshold at all. DO NOT REINTRODUCE A THRESHOLD KEYED ON TRANSCRIPT PROSE: the classifier failed because it substring-matched English the API is free to reword.

docs_coupling.$comment: A path is doc, source, or neither; doc wins. Directories match on a whole path SEGMENT, so 'docs' does not match 'src/docsify'. Data and config files (.json, .yaml, .toml, lockfiles) are deliberately in neither bucket - counting lockfile churn as a source change is how this module would become noise. Only edits made through Write/Edit/NotebookEdit are recorded; a file rewritten by a shell command is invisible.
